E. Objective Function
Our Brain-WM provides two capabilities: autoregressive
treatment planning and treatment-conditioned tumor forecast-
ing. Both tasks are supervised via a synergistic multi-timepoint
alignment objectiveL align, which regularizes the representa-
tion to remain anatomically consistent and progression-aware.
During training, we employ an alternating optimization
strategy, randomly assigning each mini-batch to either the
planning or imaging branch. We rely on the patient state
Sp = (x p,c p)at clinical timep, where the textual context
cp aggregates treatment history and demographics.
For treatment planning, we formulate the planning task
as autoregressive next-token prediction. Conditioned on the
current stateS p, the model minimizes the negative log-
likelihood of the next-step treatment planc planp+1, regularized

1) Datasets:To ensure robust model generalization across
diverse clinical settings, we curated our data from multi-
ple institutions. The internal cohort was aggregated from
three public datasets: LUMIERE [32], MU-Glioma Post [33],
and UCSF-ALPTDG [34], yielding 527 subjects with 1,659
longitudinal timepoints. To maximize temporal diversity, we
employed a dense pairing strategy, treating every distinct
timepoint pair within a subject as an independent instance.
This yielded 3,252 pairs; we used an 8:2 subject-level split
for training and internal validation, such that all derived pairs
from the same subject were confined to a single split. For
external evaluation, we applied the same pairing protocol to an
independent validation cohort of 61 subjects (128 timepoints)
from the RHUH-GBM [35] and UCSD-PTGBM [36] datasets,
deriving 72 data pairs. This external cohort offered a comple-
mentary distribution of clinical states, providing a rigorous test
for domain generalization: while the internal cohort spans the
full spectrum of the GBM treatment pathway, RHUH-GBM
is enriched for surgery-related timepoints, whereas UCSD-
PTGBM primarily comprises cases under active monitoring.
Each timepoint included 3D MRI sequences (FLAIR, T1CE,
T2W) and tumor masks.
2) Preprocessing:Treatment plans and temporal intervals
were organized from the official clinical metadata using
ChatGPT-5.1 [37], followed by manual verification to guaran-
tee data fidelity. All MRI scans were processed using a unified
pipeline prior to model training. The protocol comprised four
standardized steps [38], [39]: (1) skull-stripping to remove
non-brain tissue, (2) spatial registration to a common SRI24
template space [40] to align anatomical structures, (3) cropping
a fixed 3D volume of interest (192×192×140voxels) centered
on the brain to remove the non-informative background, and
(4) per-subject intensity preprocessing that removes outliers
and rescales intensities to[−1,1]for stable optimization.

pretrained weights of Show-o2 [21], a unified multimodal

branches and 14 task-specific layers. Specifically, intermediate

3) Implementation Details:Our Brain-WM builds on the
pretrained weights of Show-o2 [21], a unified multimodal
model that uses Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct [41] as the language
backbone. Our network comprises 28 transformer layers, struc-
tured as 14 shared layers between the planning and generation
branches and 14 task-specific layers. Specifically, intermediate
features from the shared layers at index setL={4,10,14}
are extracted and fed into the mask aligner. We optimized
the model using AdamW [42] in bfloat16 mixed precision via
DeepSpeed, employing decoupled learning rates (4×10 −5 for
LoRA adapters and2×10 −5 for the flow head, projection
layers, and planning tokens) with a warmup schedule of
50 steps and a weight decay of 0.01. Following established
configurations in unified multimodal models [21], [43], we
set the weightλ img = 4. Standard 3D augmentations (flips,
translations, and zooming) [44] were applied during training.
4) Evaluation Metrics:Performance evaluation was con-
ducted across two tasks. For treatment planning, we for-
mulated the problem as multi-class classification [57] and
compared predictions with clinical references using accuracy,
F1-score, specificity, and precision. For future MRI generation,
we assessed reconstruction fidelity [58], [59] via voxel-wise
normalized mean squared error (NMSE), peak signal-to-noise
ratio (PSNR), and structural similarity index (SSIM).

We acknowledge
that the current version presents a simplified modeling of
intervention tasks, prioritizing macroscopic tumor evolution
over fine-grained radiotherapeutic dosimetry. Future work will
seek to address this limitation by incorporating radiation dose
maps and molecular biomarkers to further enrich the patient-
specific digital twin. Moving forward, we plan to prospectively
evaluate Brain-WM to assess its clinical utility as a human-
in-the-loop decision-support tool for precision oncology.

capability_assessments.rationale: Shared MRI/clinical context feeds next-treatment token prediction and a specified-treatment/interval-conditioned future MRI flow model. L2 is evaluated conditional successor generation; label classification does not establish a model-coupled optimizer or clinical benefit.

gate_assessments.rationale: Data availability, leakage and source split assumptions require audit; no gate pass inferred.

legacy_cells.S: Given the current GBM MRI and clinical history, what future MRI is forecast under a specified treatment, and what next-step plan is predicted?
legacy_cells.T: GBM subjects with longitudinal MRI and clinical treatment metadata; internal cohort 527 subjects, external cohort 61 subjects.
legacy_cells.V: Explore/predict a next-step treatment plan and forecast tumor MRI under a specified treatment.
legacy_cells.AI: 3D multiparametric MRI (FLAIR, T1CE, T2W); clinical text (demographics, treatment history/plans); pair-specific forecast interval τ.
legacy_cells.AJ: 3D Wan2.1 VAE with distilled SigLIP semantic layers/projectors; Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct language backbone; 28-layer Transformer.
legacy_cells.AK: Pretrained Show-o2 weights; Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct language backbone; 3D Wan2.1 VAE; distilled SigLIP semantic layers.
legacy_cells.AM: Interleaved MRI/text token sequence with unified self-attention in shared layers, then task-specific Y-shaped branches.
legacy_cells.AZ: MM-Align produces tumor-subregion masks (edema, enhancing tumor, non-enhancing tumor core); mask predictions/focus regions are visualized.
legacy_cells.BA: Multi-timepoint mask-alignment objective applies focal and Dice losses to current/future tumor masks to anchor anatomical consistency.
legacy_cells.BD: Treatment-category tokens [SUR], [CRT], [RT], [TMZ], [AM], plus pair-specific interval τ expressed in days.
legacy_cells.BL: Pair-specific forecasting interval τ; case examples include 92 and 448 days.
legacy_cells.BS: Future 3D MRI (FLAIR, T1CE, T2W) generated by the flow head; auxiliary predicted tumor masks.
legacy_cells.BT: Autoregressive next-step treatment-plan head; flow head for future MRI; mask-aligner segmentation output.
legacy_cells.BV: Treatment planning: next-token negative log-likelihood plus alignment loss; MRI generation: latent flow-matching velocity-regression loss plus alignment loss.
legacy_cells.DN: LUMIERE; MU-Glioma Post; UCSF-ALPTDG; RHUH-GBM; UCSD-PTGBM
legacy_cells.DQ: Internal: 527 subjects, 1,659 longitudinal timepoints, 3,252 timepoint pairs; external: 61 subjects, 128 timepoints, 72 pairs.
legacy_cells.DX: Treatment-plan prediction: internal accuracy 91.5, F1 90.4, specificity 95.8, precision 90.7; external accuracy 90.7, F1 83.5, specificity 85.0, precision 87.2. Abstract reports MRI SSIM 0.8524 (FLAIR), 0.8581 (T1CE), 0.8404 (T2W).
legacy_cells.EK: Internal-cohort ablations: planning-only, unified model, +Y-shaped MoT, +MM-Align; generation-only, unified model, +Y-shaped MoT, +MM-Align.
legacy_cells.EL: Authors report larger MM-Align deviations from ground-truth masks in two surgical-resection cases; interval-stratified volume correlation declined from r=0.810 (0–90 days) to r=0.551 (>360 days).
legacy_cells.FB: Clinical-timepoint state S_p=(x_p,c_p): current 3D FLAIR/T1CE/T2W MRI plus text clinical context containing cumulative treatment history and demographics; next state is future MRI under a specified next-step plan.
legacy_cells.FL: MRI tokenizer (3D Wan2.1 VAE plus distilled SigLIP/projectors) and clinical text tokenizer feed a 28-layer Y-shaped Mixture-of-Transformers with shared attention/state; task-specific autoregressive treatment-plan and latent flow-matching MRI heads; an auxiliary multi-timepoint tumor-mask aligner. No optimizer/policy using simulated rollouts is evaluated.
legacy_cells.FM: Proposes Brain-WM, a shared-latent GBM model jointly trained for autoregressive next-step treatment prediction and treatment-conditioned future MRI generation, with Y-shaped Mixture-of-Transformers and multi-timepoint mask alignment.
legacy_cells.FN: Authors report internal/external treatment-plan accuracy of 91.5/90.7 and internal MRI SSIM of 0.8524 (FLAIR), 0.8581 (T1CE), 0.8404 (T2W).
legacy_cells.FO: Authors state intervention modeling is simplified, prioritizes macroscopic tumor evolution over fine-grained radiotherapeutic dosimetry, and note surgical-resection cases show larger mask-alignment deviations.
legacy_cells.FP: Add radiation-dose maps and molecular biomarkers; prospectively evaluate clinical utility as a human-in-the-loop decision-support tool.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors say existing GBM methods are static/unidirectional or treatment-conditioned generators with limited treatment categories/small cohorts, and do not jointly model treatment planning with future MRI synthesis.
legacy_cells.FR: Action-conditioned forecasts and treatment-label accuracy do not establish identified causal treatment effects, counterfactual validity, or superiority of a recommended treatment. No optimizer/policy is evaluated using simulated rollouts, and prospective clinical utility is not shown.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M4 Action service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Pass the paper’s specified action and time context explicitly into the state-transition interface; preserve the boundary between predictive action sensitivity and identified intervention effects.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pp. 1–2: title, abstract, introduction, related work; pp. 3–5: problem formulation and methods (tokenizers, architecture, MM-Align, objectives); pp. 6–9: experimental setup, datasets, Tables I–IV, figures and results/ablations; p. 9: conclusion, limitations and future work; p. 10: references. The extracted Table II MRI-metric layout has ambiguous line/column alignment, so detailed per-model values from it were not used; headline SSIM values were taken from the abstract. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: Capability is demonstrated at L2: future MRI generation is conditioned on specified treatment, but no same-patient alternative-action counterfactual comparison with identification is reported; L3 is only the authors' claim. Treatment prediction is not an optimizer and no rollout-based decision/control experiment is reported. The MRI table extraction has line-wrap/column-alignment ambiguity; abstract SSIM results and legible Table I treatment results are used. DA is not applicable because the described system is a predictive model, not an agentic system. Evidence QA: 24/79 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (30.4%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 68 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 11 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: Next-treatment classification is imitation, not tested treatment optimization or improved patient outcomes.
No matched same-patient alternative-action result establishesL3; no optimizer/control endpoint establishesL4.
Euler50 sampling steps are not50 clinical transitions; follow-up interval-bin correlations are not recurrent drift tests.
Prospective human-in-the-loop utility evaluation is future work.
One automated Codex source-review pass with skeptical criterion check; no independent human review or experimental reproduction.
Source references/bibliography were read as entries, not retrieved as independent primary studies.
Schema/quote occurrence checks are necessary checks, not proof of clinical safety, causal identification or complete scientific correctness.
